findings.issue_text: RetrieveTopic synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job inline whenever an /embed/best request misses for a URL with no TopicEmbed yet (full feed fetch, parse, per-item queries, and on first run creating a topic for every backlog item), and the 60s throttle is keyed per embed URL so every distinct URL triggers the full poll — worker/origin amplification that should be throttled globally, not per-URL

PollFeed declares retry: false, but the inline invocation runs under RetrieveTopic's default Sidekiq retry (25 attempts), so a failing fetch redoes the whole feed poll on each retry after the 60s throttle key expires

Remote fetches (open(url).read in TopicEmbed.import_remote and open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in PollFeed) read the entire remote body into memory with no size limit and no explicit timeouts, so a slow-drip origin pins workers indefinitely and attacker-selectable large assets on the trusted host cause huge memory reads
Remote content is stored via PostCreator with skip_validations: true, which skips the max-body-length validation, allowing a giant fetched page to be persisted to the DB as a post
feed_key in PollFeed (intended for an If-Modified-Since/ETag-style conditional fetch) is defined but never used, so the entire feed is re-fetched and re-processed unconditionally every hour

The PollFeed item loop issues one TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first query plus a full-content SHA1 per item every run even when nothing changed (the sha1 comparison only prevents the write, not the query/hash work), an N+1 pattern with no batching such as embed_url IN (...)

The retrieval throttle uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire; if the process dies between the two calls the key exists with no TTL, so retrieved_recently? returns true forever and retrieval for that embed URL is permanently blocked — should be a single SET key 1 EX 60 NX (or MULTI/EXEC)

The embed loading page reloads the iframe unconditionally every 30 seconds with no attempt cap or backoff, so permanently failed retrievals cause every viewer to keep generating requests and RetrieveTopic enqueues indefinitely

Raw HTML posts (cook_method :raw_html returns raw) rendered via raw post.cooked in the embed view store and render remote HTML with zero sanitization (Sanitize is an unused project dependency), so user-controlled content at the attacker-influenced embed URL path becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic synchronously executes the entire PollFeed job inline whenever an /embed/best request misses for a URL with no TopicEmbed yet (full feed fetch, parse, per-item queries, and on first run creating a topic for every backlog item), and the 60s throttle is keyed per embed URL so every distinct URL triggers the full poll — worker/origin amplification that should be throttled globally, not per-URL

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, a miss enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (async), which then calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it executes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (not enqueued/scheduled), which fetches and parses the entire feed and iterates all items importing each (`rss.items.each ... TopicEmbed.import`). The throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed as `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so distinct embed URLs bypass each other’s throttle and can each trigger a full feed poll, causing repeated full-feed work and potential amplification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed declares retry: false, but the inline invocation runs under RetrieveTopic's default Sidekiq retry (25 attempts), so a failing fetch redoes the whole feed poll on each retry after the 60s throttle key expires

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Jobs::PollFeed` is a scheduled job with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, but `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls it inline via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (not enqueued). That means PollFeed’s Sidekiq retry policy is bypassed; any exception raised during `poll_feed` (e.g., `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network failure) will bubble up to `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` (enqueued elsewhere) and be retried under RetrieveTopic/Sidekiq defaults. Because `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles only for 60 seconds, Sidekiq retries occurring after that TTL will re-enter `perform_retrieve` and rerun the full feed poll again. This behavior is directly implied by the code paths in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remote fetches (open(url).read in TopicEmbed.import_remote and open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in PollFeed) read the entire remote body into memory with no size limit and no explicit timeouts, so a slow-drip origin pins workers indefinitely and attacker-selectable large assets on the trusted host cause huge memory reads

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two remote fetches via Ruby open-uri: `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`. Both paths lack any explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options and have no response size limits; `open(url).read` explicitly reads the entire response body into memory. This makes Sidekiq jobs vulnerable to slow-drip/never-ending responses (no overall deadline) and to very large responses causing excessive memory use, which is a verifiable DoS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remote content is stored via PostCreator with skip_validations: true, which skips the max-body-length validation, allowing a giant fetched page to be persisted to the DB as a post

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces remote content ingestion via `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, where the fetched/parsed HTML (`contents` / `doc.content`) is persisted using `PostCreator.new(..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. Because `skip_validations: true` explicitly bypasses model validations during post creation, any validation that would normally cap post size (e.g., max post length / body length) would not run, and there is no truncation/size check in the new code before saving. Therefore a very large fetched page/feed item could be stored as a post in the DB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in PollFeed (intended for an If-Modified-Since/ETag-style conditional fetch) is defined but never used, so the entire feed is re-fetched and re-processed unconditionally every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method is defined (building a Redis key based on the feed URL) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items` every time it runs, with no use of `feed_key` for caching/conditional fetch or to skip processing when unchanged. So the method is dead code and the fetch/parse happens unconditionally each run (even though `TopicEmbed.import` may dedupe per-item).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PollFeed item loop issues one TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first query plus a full-content SHA1 per item every run even when nothing changed (the sha1 comparison only prevents the write, not the query/hash work), an N+1 pattern with no batching such as embed_url IN (...)

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` per item. Inside `TopicEmbed.import`, it unconditionally does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` before it knows whether the embed exists/changed. That means each poll run performs (at least) one DB lookup and a full SHA1 hash per feed item, even when nothing has changed, with no batching like `WHERE embed_url IN (...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The retrieval throttle uses non-atomic $redis.setnx followed by a separate $redis.expire; if the process dies between the two calls the key exists with no TTL, so retrieved_recently? returns true forever and retrieval for that embed URL is permanently blocked — should be a single SET key 1 EX 60 NX (or MULTI/EXEC)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands and are not atomic; if the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will fail (key already exists) and the method will return `true`, causing retrieval to be throttled indefinitely for that embed URL. Using an atomic SET with NX+EX (or MULTI/EXEC/Lua) would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed loading page reloads the iframe unconditionally every 30 seconds with no attempt cap or backoff, so permanently failed retrievals cause every viewer to keep generating requests and RetrieveTopic enqueues indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally runs `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no cap/backoff. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it always executes `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. There is no check in the controller to avoid repeated enqueues, so if retrieval never succeeds (or is slow), each reload will enqueue another `RetrieveTopic` job indefinitely. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieve` has a 60s throttle for the *work*, it does not prevent the jobs from being enqueued repeatedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw HTML posts (cook_method :raw_html returns raw) rendered via raw post.cooked in the embed view store and render remote HTML with zero sanitization (Sanitize is an unused project dependency), so user-controlled content at the attacker-influenced embed URL path becomes stored XSS on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` where `Post#cook` returns `raw` without going through the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, where `contents` comes from RSS (`SimpleRSS.parse ... i.content`) or remote HTML (`Readability::Document ... doc.content`). Neither path sanitizes HTML; `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src`. The embed view then renders `post.cooked` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, explicitly disabling escaping. Therefore attacker-controlled HTML from the feed/remote page can be stored and rendered on the Discourse origin as-is, enabling stored XSS in the embed output.
